**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce transition proof schema version equality**

The transition proof validator only checks that `schema_version` is non-empty, so an envelope with an unsupported version (for example `"999"`) is still reported as `PASS`. In fail-closed workflows this can incorrectly accept incompatible proof formats and allow downstream readiness checks to trust envelopes they should reject; add an explicit supported-version check (as done in other validators) and fail on mismatches.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject malformed PR queue entries gracefully**

Parsing `--pr` entries casts the first token directly with `int(number)` and does not handle conversion errors, so malformed input (e.g. `--pr abc` or `--pr x:passing:present`) raises an uncaught `ValueError` and aborts the command without a user-facing validation error. This makes the operator workflow brittle; handle parse failures and return a controlled CLI error (`BadParameter`) instead of crashing.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `supporting_artifacts` validation only checks `isinstance(item, str)` (allows empty strings). With warnings/blockers present, a payload could include `supporting_artifacts: [""]` and bypass the “must be supported by artifacts” rule. Consider requiring non-empty strings (reuse `_non_empty_string` / `_string_list`) and treating empty-string entries as invalid or as missing support.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Guard wrapper dispatch when policy file is unavailable**

This new dispatch path forwards all `orchestrator.*` MCP calls into `handle_orchestrator_tool_call`, which immediately classifies capabilities from `config/orchestrator/approval_policy.yaml`; in the `task-orchestrator` container image, that config tree is not copied (and no volume is mounted in `compose.yml`), so classification raises a file-not-found error and every newly added wrapper tool returns an error instead of functioning. Add an explicit fallback for missing policy data (fail-closed decision object) or ensure this dispatch does not depend on an absent on-disk policy file at runtime.

comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block automatic allow for write/destructive modes**

Automatic allowance is computed without considering capability mode, so a capability marked `decision: allow`, `automatic_allowed: true`, and `tier: T0/T1` is treated as `allowed=True` even if its mode is `write` or `destructive`; this creates a fail-open path if policy metadata is mis-tiered and can silently enable mutation-capable tools. Gate `allowed` on non-write modes (or an explicit read/analysis whitelist) so write/destructive capabilities cannot ever auto-pass.
